    NMT mathematics: a law, not a thousand tasks

    Words: 1040

    A site that prepares you for the mathematics part of the NMT (National Multi-subject Test, the Ukrainian school-leaving and university entrance exam) by going from the law to the task, not the other way round. A task here is a law dressed up in a story, and the main skill is to take the costume off.

    Main idea of the site #

    Reference sheets with formulas are allowed at the NMT. So the exam does not test whether you remember formulas but something else: whether you know which formula to apply, when, and where it stops working. 22 tasks in 60 minutes is less than three minutes each. That is enough time if the law is recognised at once, and not enough if you try the options one by one.

    1 · How each page is built #

    1. Hook: a case where the usual blind move gives a wrong answer.
    2. Concept: what kind of object this is, in the language of mathematics.
    3. Law: a formula in a frame; below it, CorollaryA theorem derived from a law in a few lines and resting on it.To the glossary : theorems derived from it in 2-5 lines.
    4. Why it is so: a proof or a clear intuition.
    5. Limits: where the law breaks.
    6. Practice: tasks in the NMT format, each naming its law, and MethodA scheme for combining several laws to solve a whole class of tasks.To the glossary : schemes for combining several laws. Tasks of the class «Data on the figure» come in threes: read and apply, pick what is needed, read and connect.
    7. Reverse move: a task without a hint, where you name the law.

    2 · The format of the exam #

    • 15 tasks with one answer out of five, 1 point each (the options here are A, B, C, D, E; on the NMT paper they carry the first five Ukrainian letters, transliterated A, B, V, H, D, in the same order);
    • 3 matching tasks, 3 points each;
    • 4 short-answer tasks, 2 points each;
    • 32 points in all, 60 minutes, the pass mark is 5 points.

    The hardest format is the short answer: there are no options to hint at the size of the number and no protection against a blind mistake.

    3 · Thirteen blocks #

    The order of the blocks is the order in which mathematics grows: each block grows out of the previous ones. The first nine are algebra and elementary analysis, the last four are geometry.

    1. Number and operations - from natural numbers to real ones: each extension closes an operation that could not be carried out before.
    2. Ratio, proportion, percent - short in the syllabus and the most expensive in lost points.
    3. Algebraic expressions - the laws of operations written with letters for all numbers at once.
    4. Equations and inequalities - equivalence, the domain, extraneous roots.
    5. Function and sequence - a dependence as a whole, not at one point.
    6. Power, root, logarithm - one equality, three questions.
    7. Trigonometry - the similarity of triangles let loose around a circle.
    8. Derivative and integral - change and accumulation.
    9. Combinatorics, probability, statistics - counting options instead of objects.
    10. Figures in the plane - a few axioms from which logic derives everything.
    11. Measurement in the plane - length, angle, area.
    12. Coordinates and vectors - geometry through equations, in the plane and in space.
    13. Space: lines, planes, solids - almost every task comes down to a flat one.

    4 · Navigator and glossary #

    The navigator shows the whole subject through seven lenses that cut across it: language and notation, laws, proof, applicability, limits, links between blocks and the traps of NMT wording. If a block is a vertical, a lens is a horizontal through all the blocks.

    5 · Frequency of laws on the site #

    How many trainer tasks lean on each law. This is the frequency on this site, not in the NMT: it shows how the site trains, not what the exam asks. What the exam asks is shown by the slice of real NMT papers below, if there is one.

    Trainer tasks in all: 59; laws they lean on: 32.

    By block

    • Number and operations: 8 tasks, one task for each law
    • Ratio, proportion, percent: 11 tasks, most often - Law of the part
    • Algebraic expressions: 8 tasks, most often - Difference of squares and Square of a sum and of a difference
    • Equations and inequalities: 10 tasks, most often - Equivalent transformations
    • Function and sequence: 15 tasks, most often - Transformations of graphs and Vertex of a parabola
    • Power, root, logarithm: 7 tasks, most often - The definition of the logarithm in one line

    6. Square of a sum and of a difference - 4

    How to use the site #

    Go through the blocks in order: each rests on the previous ones. A block page starts with a hook, then the law and its limits, and only then the tasks. A task does not open its solution until you have answered correctly: that way you train the law, not the reading of answers.
